input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

The original file names are copied into the record before staff make a listening copy. Otherwise, the coordinator keeps the box in the pending shelf and asks the group contact to check the card; the transfer is not marked ready. This is the only route to the ready label, even when the room and title seem familiar. The coordinator does not fill in missing initials from memory. When a corrected card comes back, the coordinator adds the correction date to the intake record, then applies the same check again.

That check matters later when the center schedules listening access. Staff can offer a listening appointment only for a transfer with the ready label, and the appointment is for the listening copy, not the original device or an unreviewed file. A teacher who asks about a pending transfer can be told that the card needs checking, but staff do not promise a date for access. If the transfer remains pending, staff do not place it in the appointment list. This applies even if a teacher remembers the rehearsal clearly or says they only need to check one short passage.

The catalog record has fields for the intake number, supplied title, room, rehearsal date, arrival date, source format, file names, and performer initials when present. It also has a notes field for issues such as a missing card, a file that would not open, or an agreed device return. The notes are factual and brief, not comments on the quality of the rehearsal. Staff can write that a recording has a long pause or low sound, but they should not label the rehearsal poor or incomplete. A catalog entry can be searched by room, date, title, and intake number. It cannot be searched by an unverified performer name, so initials should not be expanded based on staff knowledge.

Groups can ask to correct a title or a date after the transfer has been recorded. The person receiving the correction adds the new information and the date of the correction, while leaving the earlier supplied wording visible in the record. If the correction changes the performer initials or rehearsal date, the transfer goes through the card check again and cannot remain ready for catalog review until the coordinator has checked the corrected card. A spelling correction to a supplied title does not by itself change the ready label. Staff should keep the correction message with the intake record, and they should not replace the original file name with the corrected title.

The archive keeps the devices and paper cards in separate places. Devices waiting for return are in the locked cabinet beside the coordinator's desk, with the intake number on a removable label rather than written on the device. Cards are filed by intake number in the gray cabinet in the records room. A card that has not arrived is represented by a blank divider with the intake number, not by a handwritten substitute. When a card is later received, it goes into that place, and the divider is removed.
